nodes.label: path(segment, child)
nodes.rationale: Prepends a static segment to every child route and composes; segments with slashes flatten, so path('api/v1', x) equals path('api', path('v1', x)).

nodes.label: concat(...routes)
nodes.rationale: The OR-combinator for multiple routes at the same level.

nodes.label: First-match-wins matching
nodes.rationale: concat is OR with first-match semantics, so two routes that pattern-match the same request leave only the first reachable. The framework does not warn about this - reviewing the routing tree is the only check.

nodes.label: Method combinators
nodes.rationale: get/post/put/del/patch/head/options each take a handler returning HttpResponse or a Promise of one. del is named that way because delete is a JS keyword.

nodes.label: completeJson
nodes.rationale: The 95% response helper - application/json with the body serialized at write time. complete and completeText cover the raw and text/plain cases.

nodes.label: redirect
nodes.rationale: Sets Location and a status (default 302 Found), but the target must stay on this origin - a relative reference. An absolute URL, a protocol-relative //host target, or a control character throws HttpError(400).

nodes.label: Open-redirect defence
nodes.rationale: Forwarding a ?next= parameter into a redirect is the textbook open redirect: the attacker sends app.example/login?next=<look-alike>, the victim logs in against the real app and the browser lands on a page asking for the password again. The framework cannot make handlers validate, so the helper they already reach for validates instead, failing closed.

nodes.label: redirectExternal
nodes.rationale: The same helper without the origin rule, kept as a separate function on purpose: grep redirectExternal enumerates every place the service hands the browser to somebody else, which is precisely the list a security review asks for. Hand it a constant or an allowlisted value, never a raw request parameter; control characters are still rejected.

nodes.label: reject
nodes.rationale: Throws an HttpError with a status, message and extras - the cleanest way to short-circuit a handler. It is typed never, so code after it is dead and TypeScript flags it as unreachable.

nodes.label: HttpRequest
nodes.rationale: method, path, headers (lowercased keys), query (already parsed), params and a Uint8Array body. path is the pathname only on every backend, which matters for anything built by appending to it - a redirect target, a cache key, a request fingerprint. Percent-escapes are left encoded; decode once, then validate.

nodes.label: pathParam
nodes.rationale: The same lookup as req.params[name] with a guard: it returns the value as a string and throws a 500 if the pattern never bound it, because that is a programming error rather than a client one.
